Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on: 

Call highlights (very high level):
- HealthBridge liked the low-latency routing and the ability to pin model versions per workspace.
- Main blockers: explicit guarantees around prompt/output storage, residency, and auditability for SOC/HIPAA flows.

As discussed, can you confirm the concrete requirements for the PII/PHI items that might be included in prompts or outputs? Specifically: 
1) Which data elements (names, MRN, SSN, PHI fields) do you consider disallowed from being persisted by any third-party inference provider?
2) Residency: you mentioned US-only for production — is that strictly us-east-1, or is multi-region US acceptable (us-east + us-west)?
3) Retention expectations: what TTL would you need for (a) system logs (auth/access/tracing), (b) prompt payloads / model outputs (if stored for debugging), (c) billing/usage metadata?
4) Audit evidence: you'll need a SOC2 extract for section 5 and an example of our logging/audit trail for a sample inference request.

Attached: DataHandling_Summary_v1.pdf (short summary of default behavior + opt-in options).

Next steps we propose:
- Michael to confirm default retention commitments and provide SOC2 extract (Monica will help). Target: Wed 11/10.
- HealthBridge to send a short redline or a list of absolutely disallowed fields (Alyssa).
- Schedule 30m follow-up with your security ops and our trust engineering.

Thanks — I’ll queue the SOC2 extract and a one-page TTL matrix.

Michael — thanks for the summary and the call earlier. Quick answers and open items from our side: 

1) Disallowed persistence: we cannot allow persistent storage of direct identifiers (SSN, full MRN, full DOB when combined with name, insurance IDs). We can accept tokenized identifiers (one-way hashed IDs) stored for up to 90 days for de-duplication, but persistent PHI (raw) is not allowed without a Business Associate Agreement.

2) Residency: production inference must be US-only. We prefer single-region hosting in us-east-1 for now due to our compliance policy, but can evaluate us-west for DR only if there is an explicit standby agreement.

3) Retention expectations (our preference):
- System logs (auth/trace): 90 days, searchable by our security team.
- Prompt payloads / model outputs: default behavior must be ephemeral (no storage). If Redwood needs to retain for debugging, that must be opt-in by HealthBridge and stored in an isolated workspace with TTL <= 30 days and encryption keys under our control.
- Billing/usage metadata: aggregate usage for billing is fine; per-request identifiers should be removed or hashed and retained no more than 1 year.

4) Audit evidence: we’ll want a SOC2 extract showing the monitored logging pipeline and a sample trace for an inference request that shows request-id, timestamp, routing decision.

I’ve attached our security checklist (HealthBridge_Security_Reqs.docx). We’re aiming to get an internal security sign-off by 11/17 if the answers align.

Best,

Forwarding Alyssa’s answers — key legal/ops notes below (action items for Ben & infra):

Quoted message:
> "Prompt payloads / model outputs: default behavior must be ephemeral (no storage). If Redwood needs to retain for debugging, that must be opt-in by HealthBridge and stored in an isolated workspace with TTL <= 30 days and encryption keys under our control."

Internal summary and proposed language for our next email: 
- Default commitment: prompts and model outputs will not be persisted beyond ephemeral caches required for inference; ephemeral cache TTLs are transient and not written to durable storage.
- Opt-in persistent storage: customer may enable an "audit/diagnostic capture" feature tied to a workspace. When enabled, stored artifacts are placed in a customer-isolated data partition, encrypted with a customer-supplied key (or our KMS with CMEK), and have an explicit TTL that can be set to 1, 7, 30, or 90 days. Default opt-in TTL should be 30 days.
- Logs and trace retention: we can offer 90-day searchable logs for security by request, with role-based access and an exportable trace for a given request-id. Note: increasing searchable retention may increase cost and requires a billing addendum.
- Residency: confirm single-region us-east-1 for the initial rollout; we can offer disaster-recovery replicas in us-west with contractual constraints.

Ben — can you confirm technical feasibility of per-workspace CMEK + TTL enforcement and a short note on how request-id traces are captured (correlation id, KV of routing decisions, timestamps)? Goal: have a one-page tech note and the SOC2 extract noted below ready by 11/10 EOD so Michael can send to HealthBridge.

Monica Patel
